chapter: Suntaug Lake Inn and Duke Ellington's band
title: Catching Rock and White's show numbers at Suntaug Lake Inn
summary: At Suntaug Lake Inn he learns show songs by seeing every Boston opening, and earns $200 from performers who visit.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah, Eddie Cantor, see, I used to play down on Suntaug Lake Inn, down in Lynnfield, Massachusetts about 17, nearly 20 miles outside of Boston.

This was around 1913, '14, '15, '16, '17, see, all the big shots, people in show business would come down to this club and Rockland White, now they were at the and I used to tell the singers, theatre,/hey, go down there and hear Rockland White, they didn't go. I used to go down, and now they had a number named 'Mississippi' and the girl used to talk it like, see, M-i-s-s-i-s-s-i-p-p-i, that used to be so hard to spell, it

almost made me cry" and I forget the rest of it, but I knew the whole thing and they came down to the theatre, down to the club one night and the waiter says, Rock and White from the show is down here.
What was the name of the show.

I don't know the name of the show, but they were in this show. Rock and White, they were a team. And this girl used to do this number, so I caught on to it and I used to go down there twice a week to learn the show, learn the thing, so they came down to the club and when the waiter come and told me that, I did the number and the man give me $200. Oh, yeah, I said, you see, you guys sit here in New York -- I mean in Boston and don't go down to these shows. I catch every show that opened in Boston, I was down there opening day to see it. And to take the numbers.
